{
  "feasibility": {
    "verdict": "PARTIALLY_FEASIBLE: Single-column ELM can simulate the local water balance (total runoff = surface + subsurface drainage) at a point, but it CANNOT reproduce a routed daily streamflow hydrograph at a specific stream gauge, because that requires spatially distributed runoff generation over the contributing watershed plus a river-routing model (MOSART/RTM). NSE against an observed gauge discharge time series is therefore not rigorously answerable in single-column mode.",
    "answerable": [
      "Point-scale daily total runoff (QRUNOFF), surface runoff (QOVER), and subsurface drainage (QDRAI) at a representative headwater location",
      "Seasonal snowmelt-driven runoff timing (snowpack SWE build-up and melt) that shapes the hydrograph in this snow-dominated basin",
      "Qualitative comparison of simulated runoff pulse timing vs. observed hydrograph rise/recession"
    ],
    "not_answerable": [
      "A true routed daily streamflow hydrograph (m3/s) at USGS gauge 12488500 (American River near Nile, WA)",
      "A quantitative NSE against observed discharge, since single-column output is a per-unit-area flux, not channel discharge, and no basin routing/aggregation is performed"
    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 3,
  "n_justification": "The American River (Naches) is a snowmelt-dominated montane basin spanning a strong elevation gradient. Three columns sample low, mid, and high elevation bands to characterize runoff generation and snowmelt timing that control the hydrograph; a single point cannot represent the basin's elevation-driven snow response. This is the closest single-column proxy given no routing capability.",
  "columns": [
    {"id": "AMR_low_1200m", "lat": 46.98, "lon": -121.10, "soil_texture": "gravelly sandy loam"},
    {"id": "AMR_mid_1550m", "lat": 46.95, "lon": -121.28, "soil_texture": "sandy loam"},
    {"id": "AMR_high_1900m", "lat": 46.90, "lon": -121.40, "soil_texture": "loamy sand (rocky)"}
  ],
  "elm_config": {
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_START": "2000",
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_END": "2019",
    "STOP_N": "20",
    "RUN_STARTDATE": "2000-01-01",
    "hist_variables": [
      "QRUNOFF",
      "QOVER",
      "QDRAI",
      "QDRAI_PERCH",
      "QSNOMELT",
      "H2OSNO",
      "SNOW_DEPTH",
      "RAIN",
      "SNOW",
      "QINFL",
      "SOILLIQ",
      "SOILICE",
      "TSOI",
      "FSNO",
      "QFLX_EVAP_TOT",
      "TWS"
    ]
  },
  "requires_capabilities": [
    "MOSART or RTM river routing coupled to ELM (REQUIRED for any true gauge hydrograph and NSE; NOT available in single-column mode)",
    "Distributed/gridded ELM domain over the American River watershed to generate spatially variable runoff for routing",
    "USGS observed daily discharge for gauge 12488500 for NSE evaluation",
    "High-resolution meteorological forcing (e.g., NLDAS-2 or Livneh) resolving orographic precipitation and elevation-dependent temperature"
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "Gauge referenced is USGS 12488500, American River near Nile, WA (tributary of the Naches River); coordinates approximate the upstream headwater bands",
    "Default GSWP3 atmospheric forcing is used as a spin-up/first-cut proxy unless higher-resolution mountain forcing is supplied",
    "A model spin-up of at least 20 years precedes the analysis period to equilibrate soil moisture and snowpack storage",
    "Reported diagnostics are per-unit-area runoff fluxes; converting to channel discharge and computing NSE would require the routing and basin-aggregation capabilities flagged above",
    "Elevation bands and soil textures are estimated from regional (Cascade Range) physiography and SSURGO-type generalizations"
  ]

feasibility.verdict: PARTIALLY_FEASIBLE: Single-column ELM can simulate the local water balance (total runoff = surface + subsurface drainage) at a point, but it CANNOT reproduce a routed daily streamflow hydrograph at a specific stream gauge, because that requires spatially distributed runoff generation over the contributing watershed plus a river-routing model (MOSART/RTM). NSE against an observed gauge discharge time series is therefore not rigorously answerable in single-column mode.
answerable: Point-scale daily total runoff (QRUNOFF), surface runoff (QOVER), and subsurface drainage (QDRAI) at a representative headwater location
Seasonal snowmelt-driven runoff timing (snowpack SWE build-up and melt) that shapes the hydrograph in this snow-dominated basin
Qualitative comparison of simulated runoff pulse timing vs. observed hydrograph rise/recession
not_answerable: A true routed daily streamflow hydrograph (m3/s) at USGS gauge 12488500 (American River near Nile, WA)
A quantitative NSE against observed discharge, since single-column output is a per-unit-area flux, not channel discharge, and no basin routing/aggregation is performed

parsed.n_justification: The American River (Naches) is a snowmelt-dominated montane basin spanning a strong elevation gradient. Three columns sample low, mid, and high elevation bands to characterize runoff generation and snowmelt timing that control the hydrograph; a single point cannot represent the basin's elevation-driven snow response. This is the closest single-column proxy given no routing capability.
requires_capabilities: MOSART or RTM river routing coupled to ELM (REQUIRED for any true gauge hydrograph and NSE; NOT available in single-column mode)
Distributed/gridded ELM domain over the American River watershed to generate spatially variable runoff for routing
USGS observed daily discharge for gauge 12488500 for NSE evaluation
High-resolution meteorological forcing (e.g., NLDAS-2 or Livneh) resolving orographic precipitation and elevation-dependent temperature
assumptions: Gauge referenced is USGS 12488500, American River near Nile, WA (tributary of the Naches River); coordinates approximate the upstream headwater bands
Default GSWP3 atmospheric forcing is used as a spin-up/first-cut proxy unless higher-resolution mountain forcing is supplied
A model spin-up of at least 20 years precedes the analysis period to equilibrate soil moisture and snowpack storage
Reported diagnostics are per-unit-area runoff fluxes; converting to channel discharge and computing NSE would require the routing and basin-aggregation capabilities flagged above
Elevation bands and soil textures are estimated from regional (Cascade Range) physiography and SSURGO-type generalizations
